title: Fleet-DAgger: Interactive Robot Fleet Learning with Scalable Human Supervision
items: robots in a fleet (100 sim, 4 real)
objective: Return on Human Effort (fleet throughput per human effort)
direction: MONO-UP: Constraint violation, then Uncertainty, then Risk (prob. of constraint violation) get priority
evidence: Abstract: 'A central question is how to effectively allocate limited human attention.'
notes: Human intervention is a near-deterministic fix, not a repeated attempt, so giving it to the riskiest robot is not E2. Baseline: Random priority. C.U.R. defined in Sec.4.

title: ThriftyDAgger: Budget-Aware Novelty and Risk Gating for Interactive Imitation Learning
direction: MONO-UP in novelty and risk (low confidence of task completion)
evidence: Abstract: 'solicit interventions only at states that are sufficiently (1) novel'
notes: Help resource, not attempts. Thresholds set to meet a target intervention budget.

title: Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners (KnowNo)
direction: MONO-UP: ask when conformal prediction set is non-singleton
evidence: Abstract: 'statistical guarantees on task completion while minimizing human help'
notes: Conformal calibration on held-out data; help is a fix, not an attempt.

title: Efficient Evaluation of Multi-Task Robot Policies With Active Experiment Selection
evidence: Abstract: 'cost-aware expected information gain heuristic to efficiently select informative trials'
notes: Estimation problem (alpha=1): EIG targets the most uncertain pairs, close to Neyman-type logic. Baselines: Random Sampling, Random Task (Sec.5). Task-switch cost is modelled.

title: Active Real-World Factor-Based Evaluation for Generalist Robot Policies
spread_rule: information gain under a probabilistic surrogate
evidence: Abstract: 'adaptively selects evaluation configurations to maximize information gain'

title: Active Fine-Tuning of Multi-Task Policies (AMF)
objective: multi-task policy performance under demo budget
spread_rule: max information gain on the expert policy
evidence: Abstract: 'collecting demonstrations yielding the largest information gain on the expert policy'
notes: Baseline: uniform task sampling. Performance guarantees under regularity assumptions.

title: Guiding Data Collection via Factored Scaling Curves (FSC)
items: environment factors (camera pose, table height, distractors...)
objective: policy success rate in new environments
spread_rule: per-factor fitted power law 1 - a(n+|D|)^b; allocate by predicted marginal return
evidence: Sec.3: 'quantifying the marginal return of collecting more demonstrations'
notes: Regime-C water-filling in practice. Baselines include Equal and Greedy ('allocate the data budget to the single factor with the lowest success rate' = LEVEL, MONO-UP); FSC beats both. Curve fitting uses about 15 OOD trials per policy (hardware cost partly outside the data budget); FSC-Proxy uses an offline metric.

title: Learning When to Quit: Meta-Reasoning for Motion Planning
objective: utility = path quality minus time cost
evidence: Sec.5: baselines 'the fixed-time strategy and the fixed-quality strategy'
notes: Per-instance stopping on predicted improvement of an anytime planner vs time cost: a Lagrangian form of marginal allocation across instances. Trained on training profiles, evaluated on test profiles.

title: Stop! Planner Time: Metareasoning for Probabilistic Planning Using Learned Performance Profiles
objective: utility of plan quality vs time
evidence: title/abstract: learned performance profiles decide when to stop planning
notes: Coded from title and search snippet only.

title: Effort Allocation for Deadline-Aware Task and Motion Planning: A Metareasoning Approach
objective: probability of an executable plan within a deadline
evidence: Abstract: 'allocate computational resources among the given options'
notes: MDP over performance profiles (probability of success vs processing time); NP-hard via knapsack; MCTS and DP_Rerun. Baselines: Round Robin and Greedy (smallest mean planning+execution time).

title: Faster Motion Planning via Restarts
items: independent restarts of PRM/RRT on one instance
evidence: Abstract: running time 'suffers from inherent instability, leading to catastrophic performance'
notes: Heavy-tailed RTD; Luby-style and new restart strategies with optimality proofs. Allocation is across runs of one instance, not across items.

title: Automatic Goal Generation for Reinforcement Learning Agents (Goal GAN)
objective: coverage of goal space (mean success over goals)
direction: NON-MONO: goals of intermediate difficulty (success between Rmin and Rmax)
evidence: Abstract: tasks 'always at the appropriate level of difficulty for the agent'
notes: Training-curriculum papers: the allocated unit is training episodes per goal/task; per-goal improvement is the learning curve. With binary goal success, the learning signal per episode scales roughly like p(1-p), so regime B applies and NON-MONO / learning-progress rules are the regime-correct ones.

title: Skew-Fit: State-Covering Self-Supervised Reinforcement Learning
objective: state coverage = goal-reaching x goal entropy
evidence: Abstract: 'maximizes state coverage'
notes: Rare-state upweighting is the objective itself (max entropy), not an attempt-allocation heuristic.

title: EPOpt: Learning Robust Neural Network Policies Using Model Ensembles
direction: MONO-UP: train on the worst epsilon-percentile of domains
evidence: Abstract: 'a form of adversarial training to learn policies that are robust'
notes: Mechanically E1 (regime C, LEVEL-only, harder gets more). But the objective is CVaR, not the mean, so the rule matches its own objective; would be E1 only for a mean-return goal.

title: Active Domain Randomization
direction: towards parameters whose rollouts differ most from reference (informativeness)
evidence: Abstract: 'which we attribute to the uniform sampling of environment parameters'
notes: Discriminator discrepancy is neither pure level nor explicit marginal gain; not flagged.

title: Emergent Complexity and Zero-shot Transfer via Unsupervised Environment Design (PAIRED)
direction: NON-MONO via regret: unsolvable environments get no regret
evidence: Abstract: 'minimax adversarial training leads to worst-case environments that are often unsolvable'
notes: Explicit warning against unbounded harder-gets-more; the antagonist makes regret vanish on hopeless environments.

title: Self-Paced Deep Reinforcement Learning (SPDL)
direction: MONO-DOWN early (easy, high-return contexts), annealed to target distribution
evidence: Abstract: 'pace is controlled by the agent'
notes: Mechanically E1 (regime C, LEVEL-only); the objective is the target distribution rather than a sum over items, so this is weak.

title: VLA-ATTC: Adaptive Test-Time Compute for VLA Models with Relative Action Critic Model
direction: MONO-UP: states above an uncertainty percentile get N=16 candidates, others 1
evidence: Sec.5: 'the uncertainty threshold is set to the 80th percentile'
notes: Per-state best-of-N action error follows a power law (RoboMonkey), so regime C at state level. Threshold set from offline-dataset percentiles, but K is ablated on benchmark success (Table 3): possible E4. Uncertainty cost not counted.
